title: 3 Nasdaq Stocks to Buy Now for Growth
summary: The Nasdaq Composite has significantly declined in 2022, primarily due to rising interest rates impacting tech shares. This article identifies three Nasdaq-listed investments—Incyte (INCY), Roku (ROKU), and First Trust Nasdaq Semiconductor ETF (FTXL)—as potential growth opportunities despite current market pressures. Each pick is analyzed for its fundamental strengths, recent performance, and future outlook.

title: Focus: Bird flu puts organic chickens into lockdown from Pennsylvania to France
authors: ['Tom Polansek and Sybille de La Hamaide']
summary: Lethal bird flu outbreaks in the U.S. and Europe have forced organic and free-range chicken farmers to keep their flocks indoors, impacting the supply of specialty eggs. This change has led to consumer dissatisfaction as shoppers pay premium prices for eggs from confined hens, who are usually marketed as having outdoor access. While some farmers resist confinement orders due to humane concerns, authorities emphasize keeping birds indoors to prevent the spread of the virus and protect flocks.

title: Amazon defeats drive to unionize second New York facility
summary: Amazon workers at a Staten Island facility voted against joining the Amazon Labor Union, a setback for the union which had recently won a historic victory at another Amazon warehouse across the street. The ALU had hoped this second win would bolster its bargaining power, but faces an uphill battle as Amazon continues to fight the unionization efforts at its first successful site. Despite this loss, an expert believes the ALU will persist in its organizing efforts.

title: Amazon to reimburse U.S. employees who travel for abortions, other treatments
summary: Amazon announced it would reimburse U.S. employees up to $4,000 annually for travel for non-life-threatening medical treatments, including abortions, if the procedure is unavailable within 100 miles of their home and virtual care is not possible. This decision makes Amazon the latest company to help employees navigate state laws restricting abortion access, following similar moves by Citigroup and Yelp. The policy, retroactive to January 1, applies to employees and covered dependents enrolled in specific health plans, regardless of whether they work in a corporate office or warehouse.

title: Woman says Amazon.com fired her because she got 'long COVID' - lawsuit
summary: A former Amazon.com Inc employee has sued the online retailer, alleging she was wrongly fired and forced to repay wages after contracting "long COVID." Brittany Hope, a former brand manager, claims Amazon terminated her for "job abandonment" and billed her for overpaid wages after she requested medical leave due to severe long COVID symptoms, which she developed after being diagnosed with the flu in February 2020. The lawsuit, filed in Manhattan federal court, seeks damages for alleged violations of federal, state, and New York City disability laws.

title: With interest rates rising, it's time to focus on MANG stocks instead of FAANG, according to Jefferies
summary: Jefferies analysts recommend focusing on "MANG" stocks (Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, and Alphabet) instead of the traditional "FAANG + Microsoft" group as interest rates rise. They suggest that MANG stocks present a safer investment strategy during the Federal Reserve's monetary policy tightening. This advice was issued prior to a Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

title: With interest rates rising, it's time to focus on MANG stocks instead of FAANG, according to Jefferies
summary: Jefferies analysts recommend focusing on "MANG" stocks (Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, and Alphabet) over "FAANG + Microsoft" as interest rates rise and the Federal Reserve tightens monetary policy. This shift is presented as a safer investment strategy during an environment of increasing rates. The article highlights the rationale behind prioritizing this particular group of tech giants.

title: Amazon announces major SoCal expansion, including 1,000 jobs in Santa Monica
summary: Amazon plans to create 2,500 new corporate and technical jobs across Southern California, with over 1,000 in Santa Monica and 800 in Irvine. These roles include positions in cloud infrastructure, Alexa development, and video game design. The expansion involves new office leases in both Santa Monica and Irvine, with additional jobs also planned for San Diego.

title: 13 Companies Offering Quantum Cloud Computing Software Services
summary: This article lists and describes 13 leading companies that offer quantum cloud computing software services in 2025. It explains what quantum cloud computing is, highlighting its role in making expensive quantum hardware accessible to a wider audience, from researchers to enthusiasts. The article covers major players like IBM, Google, and Microsoft, as well as specialized quantum startups, detailing their cloud platforms and offerings.

title: TEGNA local stations to start offering their own streaming news apps
summary: TEGNA announced a new initiative to launch individual streaming news apps for its local broadcast stations. These "Plus"-branded apps will offer live and on-demand access to local newscasts, extended live coverage, and other programming on platforms like Roku and Amazon Fire TV. The move builds on the success of TEGNA's first-generation apps, aiming to provide a dedicated local content destination for viewers.

title: Why more mall brands are ramping up their third-party partnerships
summary: Mall-centric brick-and-mortar brands like Victoria's Secret, Gap, and Skechers are increasingly forming third-party partnerships to boost sales and reach wider audiences, as mall foot traffic continues to decline. Victoria's Secret launched a beauty retail partnership with Amazon, while Gap expanded its Gap Home line exclusively with Walmart. Skechers is also aggressively growing its wholesale channels, leveraging partnerships to increase sales and market penetration.

title: Seritage Growth Properties Signs 123,000 Square Foot Lease with Amazon at The Collection at UTC
summary: Seritage Growth Properties and Invesco Real Estate announced that Amazon has signed a lease for 123,000 square feet at The Collection at UTC in La Jolla, California. This agreement is expected to create over 700 corporate and tech jobs, marking Seritage's largest office lease to date. The Collection at UTC is now 93% leased and will house Amazon on its top two floors, joining other world-class tenants.

title: Stock Splits Lead to Split Results in Trading
summary: This article analyzes the impact of stock splits on market structure, liquidity, retail investor participation, notional exposure, trade size, odd lots, and volatility in both equities and options markets. Using data from 61 stock splits since 2020, including a case study on Apple (AAPL), the Cboe team found that stock splits do not necessarily increase liquidity proportionally to the split ratio and can lead to a decrease in overall investor capital exposure, though they do increase retail investor participation. The study suggests while splits enhance accessibility, they may not always benefit existing shareholders.

title: Amazon Announces SoCal Expansion, Including 700 Jobs in San Diego
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is expanding its operations in Southern California, creating 2,500 new corporate and technical jobs, with over 700 of those located in San Diego. To accommodate this growth, Amazon has signed a lease for a 123,000-square-foot office space in University Town Center, expected to open in early 2023. The new roles include positions in cloud infrastructure, Alexa development, video game design, software engineering, human resources, finance, and IT.

title: Focus: Amazon's union: Two warehouses, two outcomes
summary: Amazon's two warehouses on Staten Island, JFK8 and LDJ5, despite being near each other and hiring from the same communities, had opposing outcomes on unionization. JFK8 voted to unionize due to worker dissatisfaction with conditions and the efforts of ALU founders who had worked there. LDJ5, a newer facility with different job roles and schedules, rejected unionization, with some workers finding the work easier and expressing concerns about union dues and goals.

title: Amazon says it has too much warehouse space. What's that mean for the broader industrial market?
summary: Amazon.com Inc., a dominant force in the U.S. industrial market, appears to have reached its maximum capacity for warehouse and fulfillment space. This development could signal significant shifts for the broader industrial real estate sector. The article prompts a discussion about the implications of Amazon's changing needs on the overall market.

title: Bridge Point Melrose Park signs big leases for new industrial development
summary: Bridge Industrial has secured its first two tenants, CEVA and Expeditors, for its new industrial development, Bridge Point Melrose Park. The developer adapted during construction to meet the warehouse needs of these major logistics companies. The 87-acre development is strategically located about six miles south of O'Hare Airport in Melrose Park, Illinois.

title: I wore this $7 concealer for 8 hours — it never creased or flaked
summary: The E.l.f. Hydrating Camo Concealer, praised by beauty gurus and customers alike, offers long-lasting, buildable full coverage for just $7. The author, Jess Sims, tested the product for eight hours in the Texas sun and reported no creasing or flaking, noting its creamy texture and matte finish. She uses two shades to highlight and conceal hyperpigmentation, recommending moisturizing beforehand for optimal application.

title: F1 Boom Lures Amazon, Dell and Oracle Into Tech-Sponsor Race
summary: The increasing popularity of Formula One, especially in the U.S., is attracting major tech companies like Amazon, Oracle, and Dell Technologies as sponsors and partners. These partnerships involve using advanced technology for car design, performance optimization, data analysis for fan engagement, and even driver wellness. This trend highlights F1's blend of technological innovation and competitive sport, driving further tech demand.

title: GXO beats Q1 estimates, raises full-year guidance
summary: GXO Logistics Inc. reported better-than-expected first-quarter results, with adjusted diluted earnings of 59 cents per share and a 14% increase in revenue to nearly $2.1 billion. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting adjusted diluted EPS between $2.70 and $2.90, and revenue growth of 11% to 15%, driven by solid volume across industries and increased demand for e-commerce outsourcing. These targets do not include the impact of its proposed acquisition of Clipper Logistics plc.

title: Embracing The Inevitable Move From Hardware To Services
summary: Dell Technologies is shifting its focus from hardware sales to software and services, as evidenced by its Dell Technologies World event. The company is expanding its Apex as-a-service portfolio, enhancing its storage software, and building multi-cloud solutions like Project Alpine to offer cloud-like consumption models and address the evolving needs of IT. This strategy aims to provide streamlined experiences, consistent data mobility, and robust cybersecurity solutions for on-premises and public cloud environments.

title: With Amazon approval, what will National Landing mean for the local tech sector?
summary: Amazon's HQ2 approval in National Landing is expected to transform the Arlington, Virginia area into a tech innovation hub, with developer JBG SMITH planning extensive housing, infrastructure, and a 5G-powered smart city. The goal is to attract new companies and talent, creating an environment similar to Kendall Square or South Lake Union, while also addressing local housing needs.

title: Office Depot owner close to decision on sale of retail business as revenue falls
summary: ODP, the owner of Office Depot and OfficeMax, is nearing a decision on the future of its retail business, which could involve a sale or spin-off. This comes as the retail division experienced a 9% decline in first-quarter sales to $943 million, attributed to 114 store closures. Despite the retail challenges, ODP's business-to-business division saw a 9% increase in sales, as the company grapples with ongoing shifts in the office supply market.

title: DevOps: Why it is now the only way to develop software
summary: DevOps is presented as a cultural shift essential for modern software development, moving beyond traditional "silos" and "waterfall" approaches. It emphasizes collaboration between development and operations teams and leverages automation to achieve frequent, seamless updates, meeting high end-user expectations set by major tech companies. The article argues that without DevOps, it's impossible for applications to remain relevant in today's fast-paced digital environment.

title: Seritage Secures Lease with Amazon at The Collection in La Jolla
summary: Seritage Growth Properties and Invesco Real Estate have secured a lease with Amazon for 123,000 square feet at The Collection at UTC in La Jolla. Amazon will occupy the top two floors of the mixed-use project, which includes Class A office, retail, and restaurant space. This expansion is part of Amazon's growing footprint in California, with Seritage CEO Andrea Olshan highlighting the quality and location of the asset.

title: Grocery giant Kroger is almost ready to deliver in Miami. How do you place an order?
summary: Kroger is expanding into South Florida with an online-only grocery delivery service, opening its first spoke facility in Opa-locka by mid-May 2022, with additional locations planned for Broward and Palm Beach counties. The company will not open traditional brick-and-mortar stores, instead operating through a system centered around its Groveland fulfillment center. Customers can place orders via Kroger's website or app, with a delivery fee of $9.95 or free delivery for Boost members, and drivers do not accept tips as they are paid a "great wage."

title: Howard Schultz rolls out wage boost for Starbucks workers as union efforts gain steam
summary: Starbucks interim CEO Howard Schultz announced new worker benefits that would be available only at nonunion stores during his first call with investors since returning to the company's helm. This move comes as union efforts among Starbucks workers continue to gain momentum, and the company has faced multiple NLRB complaints alleging anti-union activities. The announcement is seen as a strategic response to the growing unionization movement within Starbucks.

title: Shopify acquires shipping logistics startup Deliverr for $2.1B
summary: Shopify announced its acquisition of Deliverr, an e-commerce fulfillment startup, for $2.1 billion in cash and stock, marking its largest acquisition to date. This deal aims to create an end-to-end logistics platform for merchants by integrating Deliverr's technology with the Shopify Fulfillment Network. The acquisition will also power Shopify's new "Shop Promise" service, offering two-day and next-day delivery, and is seen as a strategic move to compete with Amazon in the rapidly growing logistics market.

title: BNPL: Affirm to Become First Buy Now, Pay Later Partner “Fully Integrated” to Carat from Fiserv
summary: Affirm and Fiserv have partnered, making Affirm the first Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) provider fully integrated into Fiserv's Carat operating system. This collaboration will allow Fiserv's enterprise merchant clients to seamlessly offer Affirm's Adaptive Checkout, providing consumers with flexible payment options. The partnership aims to help merchants attract new customers and boost sales by meeting the growing demand for BNPL services.

title: Quantum computing firm IonQ hit by short seller report
summary: Quantum computing firm IonQ has been targeted by short seller Scorpion Capital, which called the company's claims of having the world's most powerful quantum computer "a hoax" and a "quantum Ponzi scheme." The report prompted a significant drop in IonQ's share price. Despite this, IonQ has garnered investment from major companies like Samsung, Amazon, and Google, and has partnerships with firms such as Hyundai Motor to apply quantum computing to various industries.

title: 2022 Selloff Has Left the U.S. Stock Market Undervalued
summary: The 2022 stock market selloff has pushed the broad U.S. equity market into undervalued territory, trading at a 12% discount to fair value according to Morningstar's equity research. While value stocks remain attractive, growth stocks, particularly small-caps, now offer significant discounts after substantial declines. The article highlights undervalued opportunities in the Communications, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, and Technology sectors, despite ongoing headwinds like slowing economic growth, Federal Reserve tightening, rising interest rates, and inflation.

title: A Look At The Exploitation Uber Eats Food Couriers In South Africa Face
summary: This article examines the exploitation faced by Uber Eats food couriers in South Africa, mirroring a global issue within the gig economy. Drivers report significant pay cuts, long arduous hours, and a lack of benefits or support following accidents, contrasting with Uber's claims of prioritizing their well-being. The piece highlights the precarious nature of their "independent contractor" status, advocating for regulation and drawing parallels to a recent UK Supreme Court ruling that reclassified Uber drivers as workers.

title: BREAKING: Arlington landing Boeing corporate headquarters
summary: Aerospace and defense giant Boeing is moving its corporate headquarters from Chicago to Arlington, Virginia. The move brings the company's senior executives closer to government decision-makers in Washington D.C. and includes plans for a new research and technology hub in the area. Virginia officials, including Sen. Mark Warner and Gov. Glenn Youngkin, actively lobbied for the move, highlighting the region's strategic advantages and skilled workforce.

title: Tech sell-off pushes Nasdaq to steepest drop since June 2020
summary: A tech sell-off on Thursday, May 5, 2022 pushed the Nasdaq Composite to its steepest drop since June 2020, wiping out hundreds of billions in market value. This downturn was driven by disappointing earnings reports from cloud and e-commerce companies like Shopify, Amazon, and Meta, coupled with investor concerns following the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike to combat inflation. The rotation out of tech began in late 2021 due to inflation fears and escalated with events like Russia's invasion of Ukraine, leading to significant year-to-date losses for many "Covid winner" stocks.

title: AES announces deals to provide 450 MW of renewable energy to Amazon
summary: The AES Corporation announced two Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with Amazon to provide 450 MW of solar and 225 MW of 4-hour battery energy storage. These projects will support Amazon's goal to power its global operations with 100% renewable energy by 2025 and achieve net-zero carbon by 2040. AES has partnered with Fluence for energy storage solutions for one of the projects.

title: Boeing to move headquarters from Chicago to Virginia
summary: Boeing announced it will relocate its global headquarters from Chicago to Arlington, Virginia, and establish a new research and technology hub there. This move is intended to improve relationships with customers, federal regulators, and lawmakers, especially following issues with the 737 MAX and other programs. Critics, however, view the frequent relocations as indicative of Boeing prioritizing short-term profits and access to government over engineering excellence.

title: Amazon fires managers at its pro-union New York City warehouse
summary: Amazon fired managers at its JFK8 warehouse in New York City after workers successfully voted to join the Amazon Labor Union (ALU). While Amazon stated the changes were due to evaluating operations and leadership, reports suggest six managers were dismissed because the union won the election. Amazon is currently fighting to overturn the union election results.

title: Ankur Bhatia | CEO | Chogori India Retail Limited
summary: Ankur Bhatia, CEO of Chogori India Retail Limited (CIRL), discusses the sportswear market and Columbia Sportswear's expansion in India. He highlights the company's increasing focus on sourcing from India in line with the "Make in India" initiative and outlines plans to open one store per month in tier 1 and 2 cities. Bhatia also touches upon the global sportswear market growth, the importance of sustainable practices, and the company's strategy to introduce specialized outdoor gear to the Indian market.

title: 7 Charts for Making Sense of These Markets
summary: This article analyzes current market volatility through seven charts, highlighting the Federal Reserve's aggressive interest rate hikes as a primary driver. It discusses the impact on both stock and bond markets, the underperformance of growth stocks versus value stocks, and offers insights on potential opportunities for investors amidst the market adjustments.

title: 20 trustworthy online money-making sites in Kenya in 2026
summary: This article lists 20 trustworthy online platforms where Kenyans can earn money, detailing various opportunities such as freelancing, affiliate marketing, online surveys, and AI training. It provides guidance for beginners on how to get started, emphasizing that many platforms require minimal skills and can lead to significant income with consistent effort. The article also touches on how to earn money specifically via M-Pesa and clarifies which sites are legitimate for making money online in Kenya.

title: The Old Tech FAANG Is Dulled, But a New Version Has Promise
summary: Bank of America strategists have introduced "FAANG 2.0," a new grouping of sectors designed for a world facing inflation, war, and geopolitical shifts, replacing the underperforming original tech FAANG stocks. This new version, comprising fuels, aerospace and defense, agriculture, nuclear and renewables, and gold and metals/minerals, has shown significantly better market performance year to date compared to both the S&P 500 and the original tech FAANG stocks. The article highlights the rationale behind this shift, citing energy security, increased military spending, rising food prices, and gold's role as a refuge asset in the current global climate.

title: Starbucks asks White House for equal time after Biden met with union leaders
summary: Starbucks has requested a meeting with the Biden administration after the White House hosted unionized workers without inviting Starbucks officials, expressing concern that the meeting did not represent the majority of its employees who oppose unionization. This comes as the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) issued a complaint alleging misconduct by Starbucks against union members, which Starbucks denies. Workers United, representing Starbucks employees, stated they were honored to represent all partners at the White House meeting.

title: AES Corp seals two renewable PPAs with Amazon
summary: The AES Corporation has signed two Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with Amazon to deliver renewable energy to the CAISO market. These agreements involve 450MW of solar and 225MW of 4-hour duration battery energy storage projects, helping Amazon achieve its goal of powering global operations with 100% renewable energy by 2025. With these projects, Amazon further solidifies its position as the largest corporate buyer of renewable energy, advancing its commitment to net-zero carbon by 2040.

title: Holy-Moly Mortgage Rates Hit 5.64%, 10-Year Treasury Yield 3.12%, Long-Term Treasury Bond Fund Gets Massacred
summary: Mortgage rates have surged to 5.64%, the highest since 2009, as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 3.12%. This has led to a significant increase in monthly mortgage payments, impacting housing demand. A long-term Treasury bond ETF has plunged, indicating a "bond massacre" for investors who previously viewed bonds as a conservative investment.

title: 15 Top Cities for Machine Learning Engineer Salaries
summary: This article identifies the top 15 U.S. cities offering the highest salaries for Machine Learning Engineers, based on data from Blind. It highlights that major tech hubs like Silicon Valley and Seattle lead due to high demand from companies like Meta and Apple. The piece also notes the increasing importance and compensation for AI and machine learning skills across industries.

title: Telesat, Globalstar, Intelsat headline upheavals in satellite industry
summary: The satellite communications industry is undergoing significant changes, with major providers like Telesat, Globalstar, and Intelsat experiencing corporate upheavals, new leadership, and project adjustments. These developments underscore the evolving role of satellites in global telecommunications, moving from a relatively minor component to a potentially prominent one due to innovations from companies like OneWeb and SpaceX. These shifts also highlight a broader trend where various companies, including large telecom providers, are

title: Not working out: Peloton plunges after cutting outlook
authors: ['Mark Gurman and Michael Tobin and Bloomberg']
summary: Peloton Interactive Inc. shares tumbled after the company reported a deeper loss than analysts predicted, cut its revenue guidance, and secured a $750 million debt deal. The company, which thrived during the early pandemic, is now facing "softer demand" and continued stock decline despite leadership changes and cost-cutting measures. CEO Barry McCarthy is focused on increasing subscribers and expanding the digital app, while some investors are pushing for a sale of the company amidst its financial struggles.

title: Prologis offers to buy Duke Realty in $23.7 billion deal as warehouse demand soars
summary: Prologis Inc has offered to acquire Duke Realty Corp in an all-stock deal valued at $23.7 billion to capitalize on the surging demand for industrial warehouse space. The offer values Duke at $61.68 per share, representing a 29% premium, as Prologis seeks to maintain its growth amid a tight supply chain and increased e-commerce activity from companies like Amazon.

title: Rackspace is looking to sell itself and exit the public markets, again
summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. is exploring a sale of all or part of its business to return to private ownership, less than two years after re-entering the public market. The company believes a sum-of-the-parts valuation could exceed its current enterprise value, driven by attractive growth in its public cloud sector. This move follows tepid first-quarter financial results, with a net loss of $64 million and modest revenue growth, prompting concerns about its growth trajectory in comparison to the broader cloud market.

title: Intel engineer, running for Congress, mounts union drive at Oregon chip factory
summary: An Intel engineer and congressional candidate, Matt West, is leading a unionization effort for hundreds of his colleagues at Intel's Hillsboro semiconductor factories in Oregon. The drive aims to address issues like long hours, pay disparities, and job security, particularly for engineers working on temporary visas. This initiative comes amidst a broader resurgence of organized labor in the US and during Intel's push for increased domestic chip manufacturing.

title: Google Cloud launches AlloyDB, a PostgreSQL-compatible database for mission-critical workloads
summary: Google Cloud has introduced AlloyDB, a new fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible relational database service designed for mission-critical workloads. Unveiled at Google I/O, AlloyDB is built on open-source PostgreSQL and Google Cloud's infrastructure, aiming to offer superior performance, scalability, and reliability compared to standard PostgreSQL and AWS Aurora. It emphasizes transparent pricing without I/O charges and includes AI/ML capabilities for management and analytical acceleration, positioning it as a strong competitor to Oracle and AWS in the database market.

title: Rackspace for sale, looking for privatization
summary: Rackspace Technology, which went public less than two years ago, is seeking privatization due to its market capitalization not reflecting the company's true value. The company, which helps businesses manage cloud environments, needs to make strategic changes to better compete in the growing multicloud market. Although profitable, Rackspace's growth isn't fast enough to satisfy stock market analysts, making privatization an attractive option to allow for necessary repositioning in the market.

title: Rackspace CEO’s comments fuel speculation about another sale of tech company
summary: Rackspace Technology CEO Kevin Jones' recent comments to analysts have sparked speculation about a potential sale or restructuring of the company. Jones indicated that a "sum of the parts valuation" could exceed Rackspace's current enterprise value, leading to considerations of strategic alternatives. While Rackspace later downplayed a full sale, the company is exploring reorganizing its on-premise server and public cloud services into separate entities to "unlock value."

title: How Sonos’ new voice assistant could take on Alexa and Google Assistant
summary: Sonos is launching its own voice assistant on June 1, focusing specifically on audio playback, which will support multiple music services. Unlike general-purpose assistants, Sonos Voice Control processes commands on-device for improved privacy and responsiveness. The company believes this specialized approach, combined with new hardware like the Sonos Ray soundbar, can carve out a significant niche in the voice assistant market, especially as adoption for broader smart speakers shows signs of slowing.

title: Summer’s Eve Intimate Skin Care Spa Collection Takes Serum to New Places
summary: Summer's Eve has launched a new "Spa" collection, including an intimate skin serum and a luxurious wash, to elevate daily intimate care routines. The products are formulated with ingredients like vitamin E, aloe, and coconut oil, are pH balanced, gynecologist-tested, and free from dyes, alcohol, and parabens. This launch by Prestige Consumer Healthcare aims to tap into wellness and luxury trends within the intimate care market.
source: Happi | Household And Personal Products Industry

title: Duke Realty Rejects Nearly $24 Billion Buyout Offer From Prologis
summary: Duke Realty Corp. has rejected a nearly $24 billion buyout offer from warehousing giant Prologis Inc., deeming the unsolicited proposal insufficient. Prologis made its all-stock offer public after more than five months of private overtures. The acquisition would have significantly expanded Prologis's industrial real estate footprint, which already includes over 1 billion square feet used by major e-commerce companies.

title: ReNew Appoints New CFO Also Brings in New General Counsel and Chief Growth Officer
summary: ReNew Power, India’s largest renewable energy company, has announced the appointment of a new Group Chief Financial Officer, Chief Growth Officer, and General Counsel to lead its expansion, including into green hydrogen and other clean energy segments. Kedar Upadhye joins as Group CFO, Vikash Jain as Global General Counsel, and Vikram Kapur as Chief Growth Officer, all bringing extensive experience from various top-tier companies. These strategic hires come as ReNew’s gross portfolio has surged by nearly 20% to 12.1 GW, solidifying its position as India's largest utility-scale solar developer.

title: Global 2000: Berkshire Hathaway Takes Down JPMorgan As America’s Largest Company
summary: Berkshire Hathaway has surpassed JPMorgan Chase to become America's largest public company in the Forbes Global 2000 list, driven by nearly $90 billion in profits. Despite global volatility, U.S. companies like Amazon and ExxonMobil showed significant growth, with Amazon rising to third in the U.S. and ExxonMobil rebounding strongly due to surging energy prices. The article highlights the resilience of top U.S. companies amid inflation and geopolitical challenges.

title: Starbucks Baristas Are Unionizing, and Even Howard Schultz Can’t Make Them Stop
summary: Starbucks baristas are rapidly unionizing, undeterred by the return of longtime CEO Howard Schultz. This movement is inspiring other workers, including those at Amazon, and demonstrates the growing power of organized labor. The article highlights an instance where Schultz's return was met with a mix of corporate welcome and employee activism regarding social issues.

title: Breaking Bad's Giancarlo Esposito Is The Voice Of Sonos' New Alexa-Style Assistant
summary: Sonos has announced a new voice control feature called Sonos Voice Control, launching June 1 in the US. This Alexa-style assistant will be voiced by Giancarlo Esposito, known for his roles in "Breaking Bad" and "The Mandalorian." The company emphasizes that user requests are processed locally and not sent to the cloud, ensuring privacy.

title: Giancarlo Esposito Is the Only Voice AI We'll Ever Need
summary: Giancarlo Esposito, known for his roles in "Breaking Bad" and "Star Wars," is lending his voice to Sonos's new voice control system. This system aims to compete with existing AI companions like Alexa and Google, allowing users to control music and other functions with Esposito's distinct voice. Sonos CEO Patrick Spence describes the collaboration as aiming for natural, unobtrusive, yet confident and engaging voice control, coinciding with the release of the new Sonos Ray soundbar and new color options for the Sonos Roam speaker.

title: Rackspace mulls over business unit sell-off following strategic review of company
summary: Rackspace Technology is considering selling off at least one of its business units following a strategic review that concluded the "sum of its parts" could be more valuable than the company's current form. CEO Kevin Jones stated this decision was influenced by the attractive growth profile of public cloud. The company, which recently announced narrowed losses and a 7% year-on-year revenue rise, plans to reorganize across its distinct public cloud and private cloud/managed hosting markets.

title: How Carter’s is using its Little Planet brand to test sustainability initiatives
summary: Carter's is leveraging its Little Planet brand as an incubator to test new sustainability initiatives, including eco-friendly materials and packaging. This strategy allows the large baby and kidswear retailer to adapt to growing consumer demand for sustainable products without overhauling its entire operation at once. Lessons learned from Little Planet, such as new info tags and recycled product lines, are gradually being integrated into Carter's broader brand portfolio and distributed across various retail partners.

title: Archer Datacenters Partners with Evoque to Expand Nashville Data Center Campus
summary: Archer Datacenters announced a joint venture with Evoque, a Brookfield Infrastructure Partners company, to expand its Nashville Hyperscale campus. This $200 million equity commitment aims to develop critical digital infrastructure across the Nashville and Central Southeast region, providing scaled colocation offerings with rapid delivery and a focus on sustainability. The partnership capitalizes on Nashville's significant economic and population growth, addressing an underserved market with robust power and connectivity solutions, including renewable energy initiatives.

title: USC ISI works with D-Wave to house one of the first U.S-Based Advantage™ Quantum Computers
summary: USC and D-Wave Systems Inc. have launched the first U.S.-based 5,000+ qubit D-Wave quantum computing system at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering’s Information Sciences Institute (ISI). This Advantage™ quantum system, located at the USC-Lockheed Martin Quantum Computing Center, offers academic, government, and business clients access to advanced quantum annealing and hybrid solver services. The system provides a four-fold increase in qubits and enhanced performance, furthering research in quantum simulation, optimization, and machine learning.

title: Realogy rebranding as Anywhere Real Estate
summary: Realogy Holdings Corp. announced at an Investors Day event that it is changing its name to Anywhere Real Estate Inc. The rebranding, which will be complete by the end of the quarter, is part of a larger strategy to invest in advances for consumers demanding a more seamless transaction, without directly affecting its brokerage brands' structure or daily operations. This move follows a strong 2021 and a solid first quarter for Realogy, despite a profit decline, and continued expansion of its iBuying arm.

title: Andy Burke Joins Tishman Speyer to Lead Industrial Platform
summary: Tishman Speyer has appointed Andy Burke as Managing Director, Head of Industrial, to lead its global industrial sector efforts, initially focusing on U.S. acquisition and development opportunities. Burke brings extensive experience from Terreno Realty Corporation, where he managed over 100 industrial transactions valued at over $1.5 billion. This hiring follows Tishman Speyer's recent launch of its industrial property platform and aims to accelerate the firm's growth in this sector.

title: Exclusive-Maker of Walmart, Amazon store-brand baby formulas sees shortages through rest of 2022
summary: Perrigo Company PLC, a major manufacturer of store-brand baby formulas for retailers like Walmart and Amazon, anticipates continued shortages and high demand for the remainder of 2022. The company is operating its facilities at 115% capacity and focusing on specific formulas at the FDA's request, navigating increased pressure on the Biden administration to address the widespread baby formula shortage. This shortage was exacerbated by a significant recall from Abbott Laboratories in February, with Perrigo adjusting production and pricing to meet the surging needs.

title: Starbucks in Grand Rapids votes to unionize — first in Michigan
summary: Workers at a Starbucks store in Grand Rapids have voted to unionize, marking the first Starbucks location in Michigan to do so. This decision is part of a growing national trend for Starbucks employees seeking higher wages and better working conditions. The unionization effort could help rekindle the labor movement in the U.S., especially given Michigan's past as a union stronghold.

title: WD Targets Cloud Challenges
summary: Western Digital (WD) is launching new SSDs and HDDs to address the exponential data growth and performance demands in cloud environments, particularly for hyperscale customers. The company's new 22TB and 26TB UltraSMR HDDs leverage OptiNAND and enhanced SMR technology, while their Ultrastar NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSDs target disaggregated storage in public clouds to improve utilization and density. WD also notes a strong demand for client SSDs driven by remote work and gaming, reinforcing the critical role of storage innovation across the board.

title: Exclusive: Maker of Walmart, Amazon store-brand baby formulas sees shortages through rest of 2022
summary: Perrigo Company PLC, a major producer of store-brand baby formulas for retailers like Walmart and Amazon, anticipates ongoing shortages and heightened demand throughout the remainder of 2022. This scarcity is largely attributed to a significant recall by Abbott Laboratories in February. Perrigo's manufacturing facilities are operating at 115% capacity, and the company is collaborating with retailers to ensure weekly stock allocations.

title: Sonos Ray vs Beam (Gen 2) vs Sonos Arc: Which soundbar is best for you?
summary: This article compares Sonos' three soundbar models: the Ray, Beam (Gen 2), and Arc, to help consumers choose the best option for their needs. It details the differences in design, connectivity, sound capabilities (including Dolby Atmos support), and smart features. The article highlights price points and suggests which soundbar is best suited for various TV sizes and desired audio experiences, from basic TV audio enhancement to immersive home cinema.

title: A Look Into Public Clouds From the Ransomware Actor's Perspective
summary: This article examines the potential evolution of ransomware attacks in public cloud environments, proposing that while traditional ransomware is largely ineffective, threat actors could adapt their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to be cloud-native. It discusses how attackers might gain initial access, execute attacks through control and data plane APIs, and achieve privilege escalation using IAM misconfigurations. The article concludes that public clouds are inherently more resilient to ransomware than on-premises systems, but emphasizes the need for organizations to proactively secure identities and adopt best practices to mitigate theoretical cloud-based ransomware threats.

title: QVC in the digital age: Tech giants like YouTube embrace livestream shopping
summary: Tech giants like YouTube are embracing livestream shopping, reimagining the QVC model from the 1990s. YouTube aims to streamline the existing organic behavior of users seeking product reviews on its platform by integrating live video shopping experiences with influencers. This move comes as livestream shopping has become a multi-billion dollar industry, particularly significant in China, and presents a win-win opportunity for creators and viewers by making the process easier and more interactive.

title: Starbucks to add abortion travel coverage to U.S. health benefits
summary: Starbucks Corp announced it will reimburse U.S. employees for travel expenses if they need to go more than 100 miles from home to obtain an abortion. This decision follows a leaked Supreme Court draft opinion that suggests Roe v. Wade could be overturned, leading to tighter abortion restrictions in some states. Starbucks joins other major companies like Amazon and Microsoft in offering similar benefits.

title: The PG 100: Ranking Top Food Retailers in North America
summary: The "PG 100" report ranks the top 100 food retailers in North America, highlighting an 11% increase in combined sales to $2.275 trillion in 2021. The report discusses challenges and benefits faced by retailers due to COVID-19 and rising fuel prices, as well as significant merger and acquisition activity in the industry. It provides a detailed table with sales, store counts, and top executives for each of the ranked companies.

title: Starbucks to cover employees’ travel expenses for abortions; gender surgeries
summary: Starbucks announced an expansion of its health care benefits to cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortions or gender-affirming procedures if these services are not available within 100 miles of their homes. This decision comes in the wake of a leaked draft U.S. Supreme Court opinion potentially overturning Roe v. Wade, with the company affirming its commitment to ensuring employee access to quality healthcare. Starbucks joins other major companies in offering this benefit, consistent with its history of advocating for liberal causes.

title: Amazon’s unpaid time off practices violate USERRA, class-action suit claims
summary: A class-action lawsuit alleges that Amazon discriminated against military service members by counting military leave as unpaid time off (UTO), leading to negative UTO balances and subsequent termination. The plaintiff, a former Alabama Army National Guard member, claims Amazon violated the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) when she was fired after taking military leave. USERRA prohibits employers from denying employment benefits or retention based on military service and generally requires comparable benefits for military and non-military leaves.

title: Why unattended retail is exploding in response to consumer acceptance
summary: The article discusses the rapid expansion of unattended retail due to growing consumer acceptance, driven by a desire for control and comfort in transactions. It highlights how new technologies and service concepts are emerging in various locations like sports arenas and healthcare facilities. Experts from PepsiCo, Canteen Vending Services, Aramark, and Maumee Valley Group weigh in on the opportunities and challenges, including collaboration with food delivery services and the evolving role of traditional vending operators.

title: Netflix lays off 150 employees as the streaming service contends with big subscriber losses
summary: Netflix is laying off approximately 150 employees, less than 2% of its 11,000 staffers, primarily in the U.S., due to slowing revenue growth. This move comes less than a month after the streaming service reported its first subscriber loss in a decade and saw its stock value drop significantly. The company is exploring new strategies like lower-priced, ad-supported tiers and cracking down on password sharing to regain subscribers.

title: Starbucks Labor Controversy Sparks Discussion About Unionizing and Company Reputation
summary: Starbucks is facing a labor controversy with Starbucks Workers United, which has filed numerous unfair labor practice charges against the company for allegedly interfering with unionization efforts. This situation has sparked a broader discussion about company reputation and the historical context of labor relations, with experts like Robert Josephson highlighting the importance of companies addressing employee concerns to avoid reputational damage. The article suggests that genuine empathy from leadership and effective communication can bridge the gap between management and employees in such disputes.

title: Amazon, Kong Studios Opening Offices In Santa Monica
summary: Amazon and game developer Kong Studios Inc. are establishing new offices in Santa Monica, a move city officials expect to bolster the local workforce and expand technology, game development, and corporate job opportunities. Amazon plans to open a "tech hub" in mid-2023, bringing over 1,000 new tech and corporate jobs to Santa Monica, while Kong Studios is relocating its headquarters to the city. This expansion is seen as a positive sign for Santa Monica's economic growth and its strong technology sector.

title: The Most Innovative and Important People in DC’s Tech Scene
summary: This article identifies 225 innovative and important figures in the DC tech scene across various categories including entrepreneurs, government officials, cybersecurity experts, and venture capitalists. It highlights the unique trajectory of the region's tech industry, which is deeply rooted in government but constantly evolving and expanding. The piece details key individuals and companies that are shaping the technological landscape in Washington, D.C.

title: JD.com Opens First Overseas Service Centers in the US
summary: JD.com has opened two new overseas service centers in Los Angeles and New Jersey, marking its first such venture in the overseas market. These centers will offer comprehensive aftersales and maintenance services for electronics and appliances, supported by JD's air cargo lines and self-operated warehouses in the US. The initiative aims to provide end-to-end supply chain logistics services and reduce repair times for brands and cross-border merchants.

title: US stocks suffer biggest daily drop in almost two years
summary: US stocks experienced their largest daily decline in nearly two years, as inflation concerns and the prospect of stricter monetary policy weighed on markets. The S&P 500 dropped 4%, with consumer shares plummeting over 6%, led by Target's steep fall after a reduced profit forecast. Growing hawkish sentiment from the Federal Reserve, global supply chain issues, and geopolitical tensions continue to fuel investor anxiety.

title: Goodbye, Gig Economy. It’s a Multi-Earner Era
summary: The gig economy is evolving into a "multi-earner era" driven by platforms that enable individuals to generate income beyond traditional employment. This trend has significant implications for workers, employers, and the economy, with younger generations like Gen Z actively participating in various "X-to-Earn" verticals. Employers face challenges in hiring and retention as workers seek multiple income streams, potentially requiring increased flexibility and competitive wages to attract and retain talent.

title: Netgear Orbi 6E Mesh review: A powerful—and expensive—Wi-Fi mesh system
summary: The Netgear Orbi 6E Mesh system offers extremely high throughput, especially on the 6GHz band, and generally performs very well, particularly for homes with many smart devices. However, its significant price tag of $1,500 for a three-pack and its reliance on paid subscriptions for desirable features like parental controls and extended tech support temper its overall appeal. While it outperforms competitors in 6GHz speeds, its value proposition is diminished by these additional costs, making it most suitable for users prioritizing top-tier performance over budget.

title: Why S&P booted Tesla from its ESG index
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices removed Tesla from its S&P 500 ESG Index due to a decline in its ESG rank compared to global peers. Despite Tesla's role in the transition to electric vehicles, the decision was influenced by claims of racial discrimination, poor working conditions at its factory, and its handling of a federal investigation into autopilot-related deaths. Elon Musk called ESG an "outrageous scam" in response to the decision.

title: Target Shares Plunge, Drags Down Consumer Sector ETFs
summary: Target Corp. shares plummeted after missing quarterly earnings forecasts and warning of higher costs, dragging down consumer sector exchange-traded funds. The retailer attributed the profit decline to unexpected fuel and freight costs and reiterated its commitment not to pass these costs onto consumers in the long term. This downturn also reflects a broader shift in consumer spending from goods back towards services in a post-Covid-19 world.

title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Target and growth stocks sink
summary: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Wednesday after Target's stock plummeted by about a quarter of its value, exposing concerns about the U.S. economy due to surging prices. This marked the worst one-day loss for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average since June 2020, as inflation continued to erode consumer purchasing power, impacting retailers and prompting a market sell-off. Megacap growth stocks also contributed to the decline, with the Nasdaq falling significantly, amidst broader economic worries including rising inflation, supply chain issues, and central bank tightening.

title: American Makes Microsoft Azure Preferred Cloud Provider for Airline Applications
summary: American Airlines has chosen Microsoft Azure as its preferred cloud platform for various airline applications, including airport taxiing decisions and managing operational data. This move follows previous partnerships with IBM, and American Airlines aims to leverage Azure's AI, machine learning, and data analytics to optimize customer experience and operations, particularly for gating decisions at its DFW hub. This decision positions American Airlines among other major U.S. carriers embracing cloud-first approaches for future resilience and innovation.

title: Kroger VP of Shared Services Jamie Lancaster to Present on Loyalty at Analytics Unite 2022
summary: Jamie Lancaster, VP of Shared Services at Kroger, is scheduled to present on customer loyalty at the Analytics Unite: The Summit for Retail and Consumer Brands event, taking place from June 21-23 at the Drake Hotel in Chicago. He will discuss leveraging valuable behavioral insights from loyal customers to inform various areas of the organization. Lancaster, who leads Kroger's customer contact center and support services, will be joined by Josh Blacksmith of Kimberly-Clark.

title: FedEx expands pilot of self-driving trucks
summary: FedEx is expanding its pilot program for self-driving trucks by adding a new commercial lane in Texas, collaborating with Aurora Innovation Inc. This expansion is part of FedEx's strategy to compete with Amazon in autonomous cargo hauling, following successful earlier pilots that completed 60,000 miles with zero safety incidents. The company is actively integrating autonomous technology into its operations to enhance efficiency and meet growing customer demand.

title: D-Market Elektronik Hizmetler ve Ticaret (Nasdaq:HEPS) - Stock Analysis
summary: This analysis of D-Market Elektronik Hizmetler ve Ticaret (Nasdaq:HEPS) from Simply Wall St provides a detailed overview including valuation, growth forecasts, past performance, financial health, and dividend information. The report highlights that HEPS is trading significantly below its estimated fair value with projected revenue growth, despite facing a forecast decline in earnings and current unprofitability. Key takeaways point to expanded delivery services and strategic partnerships as drivers for future success, while also noting challenges from intensifying competition and macroeconomic volatility.

title: Will smart shopping carts transform the shopping experience at Albertsons?
summary: Albertsons is expanding its pilot program for smart shopping carts, manufactured by Veeve, across several dozen stores after successful initial tests in California and Idaho. These carts allow customers to complete their shopping and checkout without needing a traditional register, aiming to enhance the grocery experience through technology. While the concept offers convenience, industry experts and commentators raise concerns about the high cost of implementation, potential user adoption challenges, and whether such advanced technology distracts from fundamental store operational improvements.

title: Broadcom in Talks to Acquire VMware, the Cloud Computing Company (Published 2022)
summary: Broadcom, a semiconductor giant, is reportedly in discussions to acquire VMware, a cloud computing company known for its virtualization software. This potential acquisition would expand Broadcom's presence in cloud computing and continue CEO Hock E. Tan's strategy of diversifying beyond chip companies following a blocked deal with Qualcomm in 2018. Following the news, VMware's stock saw a significant increase, while Broadcom's shares experienced a slight dip.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Announces New Fire 7 Tablets
summary: Amazon has announced its new Fire 7 and Fire 7 Kids tablets, which are available for pre-order and will start shipping on June 29, 2022. These tablets serve as budget-friendly alternatives to the Apple iPad mini, with prices starting at $59.99 and $109.99 respectively. The new Fire 7 boasts significant upgrades in battery life, RAM, and responsiveness compared to its 2019 predecessor, while only increasing in price by $10.

title: Edgewell Unveils New Skin Care Brand
summary: Edgewell Personal Care, known for Jack Black, is launching a new genderless skin care brand called Fieldtrip on June 6. This in-house developed brand targets Gen Z and Millennial consumers with vegan, cruelty-free products ranging from $13 to $21, emphasizing sustainability and broad appeal. Fieldtrip is expected to achieve $4 million in retail sales in its first year and will be available on its website, Nordstrom, Nordstrom Rack, Amazon, and Macy's.

title: ARKO Corp. Earns Spot on Fortune 500 List
summary: ARKO Corp., the parent company of GPM Investments, has been named to the 2022 Fortune 500 list, ranking No. 498 with over $6 billion in revenues. This marks ARKO's first appearance on the list, demonstrating significant growth and successful acquisition strategies since joining NASDAQ. Other convenience store operators like Murphy USA Inc., Casey's General Stores Inc., and TravelCenters of America Inc. also made the list.

title: Omnicom’s new supply chain tool adjusts media spend based on inventory
summary: Omnicom Media Group (OMG) has launched the Supply Chain IQ Score, a new tool designed to connect media spend with product availability. This tool uses data from over 80% of top U.S. retailers to help marketers adjust media investments based on physical, digital, and in-transit SKU inventory. The goal is to optimize media spend amid ongoing supply chain disruptions, allowing brands to shift focus to products with healthy inventory and high sales correlation, thereby improving ROI and meeting performance goals.

title: Amazon gains on UPS in package delivery volume
summary: Amazon's package delivery business, Amazon Logistics, is rapidly gaining on UPS in terms of delivery volume, having already surpassed FedEx in 2020. While Amazon Logistics held a 22% share of the parcel delivery market by volume last year, its revenue share is significantly lower at 12% due to its Prime free shipping model. Amazon plans to invest $1 billion in other logistics companies to further its growth.

title: Interxion pauses plans for $300 million expansion in Dublin
summary: Interxion has paused a $300 million expansion plan in Dublin due to a de facto moratorium placed on new data center developments in the greater Dublin area by EirGrid, Ireland's national grid operator. This moratorium, which could last until 2028, has led to calls for a nationwide ban and has prompted criticism from various industry bodies, despite local council efforts to prevent further data center construction. The situation highlights the growing pressure on Ireland's energy resources from data centers, which now consume 11 percent of the country's total grid-generated electricity.

title: Cleveland-Cliffs and TravelCenters of America return to Fortune 500
summary: Cleveland-Cliffs and TravelCenters of America have rejoined the Fortune 500 list. Walmart topped the overall list, followed by Amazon and Apple. The article also mentions other related business news.

title: Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index Finds US Parcel Volume Reached Record High of 21.5 Billion in 2021
summary: The Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index revealed that US parcel volume grew by six percent in 2021, reaching a record high of 21.5 billion parcels. Carrier revenues also increased significantly to $188 billion, up 16 percent from 2020. The report highlights the continued impact of the pandemic on shipping and logistics, forecasting further growth to 25-40 billion parcels by 2027.

title: Amazon.com Inc. delays hiring by months at new 1 million-square-foot facility in Clarksville
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has delayed hiring for its new 1 million-square-foot fulfillment center in Clarksville, Tennessee. The company is reportedly waiting to invest in manpower until there is a clear inbound supply of materials for the facility. This delay indicates a revised hiring schedule compared to initial plans.

title: Broadcom Inc in talks to acquire VMware: sources
summary: Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in discussions to acquire cloud-computing company VMware Inc., a deal that would significantly expand the chipmaker's software presence. This potential acquisition aligns with CEO Hock Tan's strategy of diversifying Broadcom through software companies. VMware, valued at around US$40 billion, would provide Broadcom with greater access to the data center market, a critical area for growth.

title: Caterpillar To Expand Texas Manufacturing Facility
summary: Caterpillar Inc. is expanding its manufacturing plant in Schertz, Texas, with a $24 million investment in new equipment and the addition of 24 new jobs by 2026. This expansion will bring the total workforce to 169 jobs and a payroll exceeding $8 million, supported by a 10-year agreement with the Schertz Economic Development Corporation. The facility specializes in machining engine components for various Caterpillar products, reinforcing the company's commitment to the region.

title: How Amazon, Microsoft, Costco and more Seattle-area brands rank by reputation
summary: Amazon ranked highest among Seattle-area companies in a recent Axios and Harris Poll survey assessing the reputations of the 100 most visible corporate brands in the U.S. Conversely, Costco, based in Issaquah, experienced a 17-place drop in the same survey. The article highlights how local companies performed in this national reputational ranking.

title: Walmart Expanding Drone Delivery Network to Six States
summary: Walmart is expanding its drone delivery network to serve approximately 4 million households across six states: Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Texas, Utah, and Virginia. This initiative aims to compete with companies like Amazon and FedEx in the growing speedy delivery market. The service will deliver packages up to 10 pounds within 30 minutes for a $3.99 fee and projects over 1 million drone deliveries annually.

title: UGA honors companies that hired the most UGA grads
summary: The University of Georgia recognized the top 25 employers of its Class of 2021 at an event in Sanford Stadium. These companies hired graduates across various industries, from technology and finance to retail and healthcare. UGA's Career Center provides resources for employers to connect with its diverse talent pool.

title: Our verdict on the Garmin Instinct 2S GPS smartwatch
summary: This review covers the Garmin Instinct 2S Solar smartwatch, highlighting its robust features, impressive battery life (especially the solar model), and comprehensive health and fitness tracking capabilities. The article notes its affordability compared to other high-end Garmin watches, praising its utility for keen runners and triathletes despite some limitations in music storage and advanced mapping.

title: Kroger Extends Its Delivery Reach in Ohio
summary: Kroger is expanding its delivery network in Ohio with a new 61,000-square-foot facility in Lockbourne, powered by Ocado Group technology. This "spoke" facility will serve central Ohio and act as a last-mile cross-dock location, extending delivery services up to 200 miles. The expansion is expected to create 200 jobs and further Kroger's digital shopping experience, including the Boost by Kroger Plus service for customers.

title: Zadara edge cloud surpasses 400 points of presence
summary: Zadara, an edge cloud provider, has expanded its global presence to over 400 points of presence across 24 countries, partnering with more than 250 managed service providers. Despite falling short of its 2020 target of 1,000 locations by the end of 2021, the company claims to have more edge points of presence than other public clouds. Zadara offers compute, storage, and networking as managed services and has seen significant growth in revenue and customers, funding its expansion through its own revenues and over $60 million in venture funding.

title: After worst financial quarter in years, Amazon puts plans for large distribution center in Round Rock on hold
summary: Amazon has decided to put plans for a large distribution center in Round Rock, near Austin, on hold. This decision comes after the e-commerce giant experienced its worst financial quarter in years and is looking to shrink its nationwide warehouse footprint. The move has local implications for the Austin area.

title: 100-megawatt Sunflower solar station unveiled in Mississippi Delta
summary: Entergy Mississippi unveiled the 100-megawatt Sunflower Solar Station, the state's largest solar power plant, in Sunflower County. This facility will power 16,000 homes and is the first step in Entergy's plan to add 1,000 megawatts of renewable energy over the next five years. The project highlights collaboration with Mississippi businesses and provides clean energy while offering a hedge against rising natural gas prices.

title: Hyperion looks to slower growth for a helping hand
summary: Australia's largest growth manager, Hyperion, is betting on a counterintuitive outcome—an economic downturn and anemic growth—to revive its performance. Despite a 36% year-to-date loss, Hyperion's CIO Mark Arnold believes that high inflation and high interest rates are temporary and will retreat as the economy cools, providing a tailwind for growth stocks. The firm argues that its disruptive holdings, like Tesla and Amazon, will outperform in a cooler economy where growth is scarce, forcing capital allocators to invest in companies with double-digit earnings growth.

title: Courts Are Not A Weapon: How Corporations Like Chevron Use The Law To Get Their Way
summary: This article discusses how corporations like Chevron weaponize legal systems against activists and critics, exemplified by the case of Steven Donziger. It highlights the extensive legal battle between Chevron and Donziger, who secured a $9.5 billion settlement for environmental destruction in Ecuador, and details the subsequent corporate retaliation he faced. The piece advocates for shareholders, investors, and governments to promote corporate social responsibility and prevent the misuse of legal processes to suppress dissent, emphasizing a zero-tolerance approach to retaliation against human rights defenders.

title: Coty launches first-ever Chloé Fragrances e-commerce store
summary: Coty Inc. has launched the first-ever Chloé Fragrances digital store in partnership with e-commerce platform Lazada. The digital store, hosted on LazMall Prestige, will feature Chloé Signature and Nomade lines, along with exclusive launch sets and will be supported by a digital marketing campaign and a live stream event. This move is part of Coty's strategy to expand its premium digital footprint across Southeast Asia, leveraging the growth in luxury e-commerce.

title: Tech Moves: Elizabeth Scallon departs Amazon for HP; Fauna hires marketing exec; and more
summary: Elizabeth Scallon, a Seattle tech veteran from Amazon, has moved to HP as director of Incubation enablement. Fauna has hired John Novak as vice president of marketing, and Blueprint Technologies brought on Gary McMath as chief of growth. Several other tech companies, including NAVEX and Unbounce, also announced significant personnel changes across leadership roles in the Pacific Northwest tech community.

title: Broadcom will tame the VMware beast
summary: Broadcom's planned acquisition of VMware for $61 billion signifies a new era for the virtualization leader, focusing on financial performance and shareholder value. The article details Broadcom's strategy of optimizing profitability by focusing on recurring revenue, cutting R&D and sales/marketing expenses for less profitable areas, and standardizing G&A. For customers, this likely means higher prices and a more focused product portfolio, with core offerings like vSphere being emphasized while less profitable or unproven ventures like Project Monterey face scrutiny.

title: Putting Recent Market Volatility in Perspective
summary: This article provides perspective on recent market volatility, noting that while 2022 has been a bumpy ride for investors with significant downturns in growth stocks and technology, such fluctuations are not historically uncommon. It examines the CBOE VIX Index and standard deviation data to show increased volatility, driven by inflation fears and rising interest rates, but emphasizes that market losses are a normal part of investing. The piece concludes by advising long-term investors to maintain their asset mix and avoid drastic changes unless retirement or significant near-term expenses necessitate a re-evaluation of their portfolio.

title: How Chatbots are Revolutionizing Customer Experience
summary: Modern AI-powered chatbots are transforming customer experience by handling various tasks from ordering taxis to booking appointments, driven by advancements in AI, Machine Learning, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Unlike traditional rule-based bots, NLP allows chatbots to understand complex conversations, retain context, and interpret human sentiment by integrating with external knowledge sources. Conversational AI, built on neural networks, enables chatbots to learn and improve continuously, process vast amounts of unstructured data to predict user behavior, and perform repetitive tasks, making them indispensable for businesses and freeing up human employees for more complex issues.

title: GM steals executive back from Amazon to lead global workplace safety
summary: General Motors has appointed Marcos Purty as its new vice president of Global Workplace Safety, replacing the retiring Jim Glynn. Purty returns to GM from Amazon, bringing 25 years of prior experience with GM, including various leadership roles in manufacturing and strategy. His critical mandate will be to enhance workplace safety across all GM facilities and to support the company's transformation towards all-electric vehicles and carbon neutrality.

title: Five Below opening location in East Setauket this summer
summary: Five Below is set to open a new store in East Setauket on July 1st, located in the Suffolk Plaza shopping center. The store will occupy approximately 20,000 square feet next to a future Amazon Fresh, in a space previously housing a Waldbaum’s grocery store. This new location will bring low-cost products to the community and is also hiring staff.

title: Moderna CEO Joins List of Billionaires Committed to Philanthropy
summary: Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel announced his plan to exercise 4.59 million stock options and donate the estimated $355 million in proceeds to charity, a process expected to take about a year. He cited a Jesuit background and the principle of servant leadership as motivations, and his intentions align with other billionaires like MacKenzie Scott, Bill Gates, and Warren Buffett who have pledged significant portions of their fortunes to philanthropy. Bancel emphasized transparency regarding these sales and confirmed he will be using a trading plan to mitigate impact on Moderna's stock price.

title: Boeing will move global HQ to Arlington
summary: Boeing announced its decision to relocate its global headquarters from Chicago to its existing campus in Arlington, Virginia. This move will make Boeing the largest defense contractor headquartered in Virginia, leveraging its proximity to government stakeholders and a skilled workforce. The company also plans to develop a research and technology hub in Arlington, supported by a significant gift to Virginia Tech.

title: Industry backs Lloyd’s of London’s $465m DXC Technology contract extension
summary: The insurance industry has largely welcomed Lloyd’s of London's $465 million contract extension with DXC Technology, viewing it as a crucial step towards digital transformation. This agreement aims to modernize Lloyd's IT systems by transitioning around 400 London market insurance companies to a cloud-native digital platform running on Amazon Web Services. This move is expected to significantly improve speed, efficiency, and operational resilience, transforming the market from a paper-based system to a data-focused, automated, and cost-efficient one.

title: iRobot Unveils iRobot OS - The Most Thoughtfully Intelligent Operating System for the Home
summary: iRobot has launched iRobot OS, a new operating system that enhances the intelligence of its home robots. This OS integrates advanced computer vision and machine learning to offer features like improved pet-centric cleaning, object avoidance, and enhanced voice command capabilities for Roomba j7 and j7+ robot vacuums. iRobot OS is designed to make robot cleaning more effective and adapt to user preferences and home environments.

title: American Eagle’s Quiet Platforms partners with global shipper Pitney Bowes
summary: American Eagle's logistics platform, Quiet Platforms, has partnered with global shipper Pitney Bowes to enhance its delivery and fulfillment capabilities. This collaboration aims to offer faster delivery services and logistics to its network of retailers and brands, strengthening Quiet Platforms' position as an "anti-Amazon" open-sharing logistics model. The partnership will leverage Pitney Bowes' Designed Delivery service to customize delivery networks for Quiet Platforms' clients like Steve Madden, Kohl’s, and Peloton.

title: ZIM Logistics China (ZLC), Ladingo and ZIM Announce the Launch of ZL MAX™ - a New Service Package for Amazon Sellers and eCommerce Businesses
summary: ZIM Logistics China (ZLC), Ladingo, and ZIM Integrated Shipping Services have partnered to launch ZL MAX™, a new comprehensive service package designed for Amazon sellers and eCommerce businesses operating on the China-US West Coast trade route. This service provides end-to-end logistics, including a dedicated digital platform from Ladingo for instant quotes and LCL shipment booking, and leverages ZIM's eCommerce Xpress Service for fast transit times. The collaboration aims to offer reliable, digital, and efficient cross-border shipping solutions amidst growing eCommerce demand and supply chain challenges.
